rationale: The base station is online locally (uplink_status ok, all 7 devices online, local streams and local app sessions work), but the event log shows repeated E-503 "cloud reporting failed" and the customer reports remote notifications stopped. Frontline steps (mesh firewall disabled, nodes rebooted, base station power-cycled, DNS automatic) did not resolve it, matching the KB escalation criteria for a persistent cloud-channel/certificate issue.

output.symptom_summary: Customer reports remote notifications stopped after installing a new mesh Wi-Fi system. Local camera and sensor functionality works, but events are not reaching the cloud.
output.suspected_root_cause: Persistent cloud-channel or certificate issue causing E-503 cloud reporting failures despite local network connectivity.
key_abnormal_indicators: Error code E-503 'cloud reporting failed' repeatedly in logs
Local streams and local app sessions work
Frontline steps (mesh firewall disabled, nodes rebooted, base station power-cycled, DNS automatic) did not resolve
output.customer_reply: Thank you for your patience. We've identified that your base station is having trouble communicating with our cloud service, which is why remote notifications have stopped. I've escalated your case to our engineering team for further investigation. They will follow up with you shortly. No further action is needed from you at this time.

args.query: E-503 uplink blocked events not reaching cloud

args.question: Is the base station connected to the new mesh system by Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi? And when you open the app while away from home (on mobile data), can you see live view, or does everything fail remotely?

args.action: Power-cycle the base station: unplug its power for 30 seconds, then plug it back in and wait 2 minutes. Also, in the mesh router app, set the DNS to "Automatic" (not a custom/ISP DNS). Then tell me whether the E-503 / notification issue clears.

args.query: E-503 uplink blocked events not reaching cloud

results.text: Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.
